citation: R. Mohan, S. Sundararaj, K. B. Thiagarajan, 'Numerical simulation of flow over buildings using OpenFOAM', AIP Conf. Proc. 2112, 020149 (2019).
context: The paper is a qualitative CFD demonstration using the OpenFOAM v1906 simpleFoam/windAroundBuildings tutorial verbatim (nu=1.5e-5 m^2/s, U_inlet=10 m/s, k-epsilon, TI=0.1, steady RANS/SIMPLE, ~185k cells). Only contour plots, streamlines, and LIC images are shown; no quantitative or experimental validation is provided.

open_questions.q: Does the qualitative flow topology (roof acceleration, wake recirculation length, 3D wake spread) reported by steady RANS k-epsilon change materially when the same geometry is solved with LES at the same effective inlet Reynolds number (Re ~ 10^7 based on building height ~15 m, U=10 m/s, nu=1.5e-5)?
open_questions.basis: The paper uses standard k-epsilon, which is known to under-predict separation and over-predict TKE at sharp bluff-body edges (stagnation-point anomaly). Our replication measured max k = 27.84 m^2/s^2 (18.6x amplification vs k_inlet=1.5), max|U|=20.66 m/s at a leading-building corner, and min U_x=-9.997 m/s in the wake -- all steady-mean quantities. Whether an LES on the same geometry yields substantially different mean profiles, longer/shorter recirculation bubbles, or qualitatively different roof shear layers is untested by both the paper and by us.
next_steps: Rerun the same windAroundBuildings geometry with pisoFoam or pimpleFoam using dynamicKEqn or Smagorinsky LES on a refined (~5-10 M cell) mesh; require y+ < 1 on rooftops.
Time-average the LES over >= 10 flow-through times and compare mean U_x, U_y, U_z line profiles at the same six sample lines (inletZ, x100Z, x200Z, x300Z, z20X, z60X) used in this replication.
Publish delta metrics: |mean-U_x_LES - U_x_RANS| / U_inlet at each line, plus recirculation-length ratio.

open_questions.q: How sensitive are the street-canyon vortices, near-roof shear layers, and downstream wake recirculation to mesh resolution and to snappyHexMesh refinement level around building surfaces?
open_questions.basis: The tutorial mesh has 185,237 cells over a domain of ~350x280x140 m containing ~30 buildings, giving < 6,000 cells per building on average. No mesh-independence study is presented in the paper, and none was performed in this replication. The reported convergence (U_x res 2.39e-5, p res 4.30e-4 after 400 SIMPLE iters) is convergence in iteration space, not convergence in mesh space.
next_steps: Run a systematic mesh-refinement study: baseline (185k), 2x (~1.5M via level+1 in snappyHexMesh refinementRegions), 4x (~10M), holding all other settings fixed.
Track: max|U|, min U_x, max k, integrated drag/lift on each building, and mean recirculation length behind two representative buildings.
Report Grid Convergence Index (Roache) on each observable; discuss whether the tutorial mesh is within asymptotic range.

open_questions.q: Do the qualitative predictions (roof acceleration ratio, wake reversal fraction, lateral spread) survive quantitative comparison against wind-tunnel PIV or hot-wire measurements over a realistic urban array (e.g. CEDVAL A1-1, Mock Urban Setting Test, or Michel-Stadt datasets)?
open_questions.basis: The paper offers no experimental validation. Our replication shows: (a) max|U|=20.66 m/s at leading-building corner (2.07x inlet speed-up); (b) 29-30% of wake samples with U_x<0; (c) 3D wake with U_y, U_z swings of +/-15 m/s. Whether the same simpleFoam+k-epsilon setup, when pointed at a wind-tunnel-mapped geometry, would predict measured PIV velocity fields within accepted CFD-of-urban-flow tolerances (typically <=20% mean U, <=30% TKE per COST-732/AIJ guidelines) is completely open.
next_steps: Rebuild the case with CEDVAL A1-1 geometry (single cube in a boundary layer) and inlet boundary-layer profile matching the wind-tunnel measurements.
Compare mean U/U_ref and u'/U_ref profiles at the standard 8 vertical measurement locations against published CEDVAL data.
Compute hit-rate q, factor-of-2 FAC2, and normalized mean square error NMSE using the AIJ 2016 guideline metrics; report where k-epsilon+simpleFoam falls short.

open_questions.q: Can the same simpleFoam+k-epsilon setup be extended to solve a coupled scalar-transport problem for pollutant dispersion, and does the resulting concentration field match tracer-release wind-tunnel benchmarks?
open_questions.basis: Urban CFD's principal application is pollutant/tracer dispersion, not just velocity fields. The paper stops at velocity magnitude and streamlines. Our replication has a converged mean U + turbulent nu_t field (max nu_t = 12.48 m^2/s at rooftop shear layer) -- these are precisely the inputs a scalar-transport equation would need. Whether adding scalarTransportFoam-style passive scalars to the same tutorial produces physically reasonable concentration fields at street level, and whether those fields match measured tracer plumes (e.g. Michel-Stadt continuous point-source SF6 releases), is untested.
next_steps: Extend the case with a scalarTransport function object; place a passive point source at street level upstream of the building group.
Solve for steady-mean concentration C using the frozen U, nu_t field; compare against a well-known tracer benchmark (Michel-Stadt or CODASC continuous-release datasets).

Report concentration profiles at street level and compare hit-rate/FAC2/NMSE against measured plumes; discuss the impact of steady-RANS averaging on peak concentrations (which are unsteady-dominated).

open_questions.q: How much does replacing the paper's uniform inlet U=(10,0,0) m/s with a fully developed atmospheric-boundary-layer (ABL) inlet profile change the predicted flow around and between buildings?
open_questions.basis: The paper uses a uniform inlet velocity, uniform k, uniform epsilon -- i.e. no ABL log-law profile, no ground-roughness matching. This is academically clean but not standard practice for realistic urban CFD (Franke, Blocken, Tominaga COST-732 / AIJ guidelines all require ABL-consistent inlet). Our replication observed inlet U_x aloft ~10.0-11.0 m/s but with a strong ground boundary layer developing near z=0 -- a spurious near-ground BL that grows only because the inlet lacks one. Whether the paper's qualitative claims (roof acceleration, wake recirculation, upstream undisturbed) hold when a proper ABL log-law inlet + matched ground roughness are imposed is unknown.
next_steps: Replace inlet U with atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity (log-law with reference height z_ref=10 m, u_ref=10 m/s, z_0=0.5 m for urban terrain) and matched atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon boundary conditions.
Add ground-patch roughness length matching (z_0 or equivalent nutkAtmRoughWallFunction).
Rerun to convergence and re-extract the six line profiles; report relative changes in max|U|, min U_x, wake reversal fraction vs the uniform-inlet case.

notes: All 5 questions are truly open: they were not addressed by the paper AND were not fully addressed by this replication. They target the paper's four principal scientific gaps -- turbulence-model fidelity (LES vs RANS), mesh sensitivity, absence of experimental validation, and dispersion/ABL extensions -- in order of increasing scope.
